title: "Your king comes to you … lowly, and riding on a donkey" (Zech 9:9–10)
speaker: The LORD (through the prophet)
description: Daughter Zion is to rejoice: her king comes, righteous and having salvation, lowly and riding on a donkey, a colt; chariot, horse and battle bow will be cut off, he will speak peace to the nations, and his dominion will be from sea to sea.

interpretations.label: Fulfilled in Jesus's entry into Jerusalem
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: Matthew and John cite the verse of Jesus's entry; Keil holds that Jesus arranged the entry to fulfil it and that the universal peace of 9:10 belongs to the kingdom he founded. Objection: Mitchell notes that Matthew follows the Greek and has two animals where the Hebrew parallelism means one.

interpretations.label: An ideal Messianic king, prompted by Alexander's appearance; the evangelists cite it freely
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: the humble king without chariots contrasts with Jer 22:4; the author saw in Alexander the forerunner of a Davidic ruler; the second part "was not fulfilled, but it furnished an ideal".
